name: M.Sc. (Agriculture) Plant Pathology
duration_note: A two-year full-time postgraduate degree (4 semesters) combining laboratory and field coursework with a supervised master's research thesis.

hero.eyebrow: Postgraduate plant disease science & diagnostics degree
hero.summary: A two-year master's programme investigating the causes, mechanisms and management of plant diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, viruses and abiotic stresses. Students master classical and molecular diagnostics, epidemiology, fungicide chemistry, biocontrol and resistance breeding to safeguard crop harvests.

overview.heading: What an M.Sc. in Plant Pathology covers
paragraphs: Plant Pathology is the branch of agricultural science dedicated to understanding plant health, the etiology and biology of plant diseases, and the methods used to protect crops against devastating pathogens. From historic famines to modern rust and blast outbreaks, plant diseases present constant threats to global food systems and agricultural trade.

Conforming to ICAR's Broad Subject Matter Area (BSMA) restructured curriculum, the M.Sc. Plant Pathology degree encompasses 70 credits: 20 major credits, 8 minor credits (often chosen from Entomology, Genetics & Plant Breeding, or Microbiology), 6 supporting credits including advanced experimental statistics, 5 common research credits, 1 master's seminar credit and 30 credits dedicated to thesis research.

The curriculum provides extensive laboratory and field training across mycology (fungal taxonomy and biology), plant virology, plant bacteriology, disease physiology, molecular diagnostics (PCR, RT-PCR, ELISA), disease forecasting, chemical fungicides, and biological control agents like Trichoderma and Pseudomonas.

highlights.label: Core laboratory areas
highlights.value: Pathogen isolation, molecular detection (PCR/ELISA), fungicide bioassays and culture collections

who_should_apply: Agriculture and horticulture graduates fascinated by plant disease symptoms, microscopic examination and microbiological lab techniques
Students eager to work in seed health testing, plant quarantine inspection and molecular disease diagnostics
Aspirants targeting scientific research careers through ICAR Agricultural Research Service (ARS) or university teaching via ASRB NET
Candidates interested in product development, clinical bio-efficacy trials and technical advisory in the crop protection industry

curriculum.heading: Course structure under ICAR BSMA 2021 guidelines
curriculum.intro: The master's syllabus integrates foundational pathogen biology with advanced disease management and independent thesis research. Course codes and electives follow the BSMA curriculum guidelines adopted by agricultural universities.

structure.focus: Core organism groups, principles of pathogenesis and disease management.
Crop-specific diseases, epidemiology, fungicides and biocontrol agents.
courses: Chemicals & Bioagents in Plant Disease Management

structure.focus: Microbiology, plant breeding, biotechnology and statistics.
Research tools, scientific communication, ethics, seminar presentation and 30-credit dissertation.

practical_learning.name: Pure culture isolation & pathogen identification
practical_learning.description: Isolating fungal and bacterial pathogens from infected leaf, stem and root tissues, culturing on synthetic media, and microscopic classification.

practical_learning.name: Molecular & serological diagnostics
practical_learning.description: Conducting DNA extraction, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification, gel electrophoresis and ELISA assays for viral and bacterial identification.

practical_learning.name: Fungicide bioassays & poison food technique
practical_learning.description: Evaluating the efficacy of systemic and contact fungicides against fungal mycelial growth using the poisoned food technique to determine EC50 values.

practical_learning.name: Controlled pot & field disease screening
practical_learning.description: Artificial inoculation of pathogen inoculum to evaluate crop germplasm for resistance against rusts, wilts, smuts and blights.

points: Successful completion of a 4-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture or B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture from an ICAR-accredited or recognized agricultural institution.
Minimum required grade point average: 6.0 out of 10.0 OGPA (or 60% aggregate) for General, OBC, and EWS candidates; 5.0 out of 10.0 OGPA (or 50% aggregate) for SC, ST, and PwD candidates.
Final semester students awaiting results may apply provisionally, provided proof of completion is submitted at the time of final admission counselling.

routes.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
routes.description: All-India competitive entrance exam conducted by NTA for admission to master's seats in central agricultural universities, ICAR deemed institutes, and state agricultural university quotas.

routes.name: State Agricultural University PG Entrances
routes.description: State exams such as UPCATET (UP), MCAER (Maharashtra), Rajasthan Pre-PG, and state university entrance portals for state domicile seats.

routes.name: Private Agricultural Universities
routes.description: Institutions offering ICAR-aligned curricula admit through university-level tests or merit-based screening.

exams.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG - Plant Science)
exams.note: 2-hour computer-based exam covering plant pathology, microbiology, genetics, and agricultural botany.

steps.title: Check eligibility criteria
steps.text: Review the current ICAR AIEEA (PG) Information Bulletin for qualification requirements in the Plant Science group.

steps.title: Register online
steps.text: Submit the online application on the NTA ICAR portal and pay the examination fee before the deadline.

steps.title: Appear for AIEEA (PG)
steps.text: Take the nationwide CBT testing your grasp of plant pathology, general agriculture and allied biological sciences.

steps.title: Counselling & choice locking
steps.text: Participate in online counselling to select your preferred university and Department of Plant Pathology based on your all-India rank.

fees.summary: State Agricultural Universities and ICAR institutes provide subsidized higher education with annual tuition fees typically between ₹15,000 and ₹35,000 for government quota seats. Students securing high ranks through ICAR AIEEA (PG) receive the ICAR PG Scholarship / National Talent Scholarship with monthly financial support. Private universities charge annual tuition between ₹60,000 and ₹1,40,000. Laboratory consumables and accommodation charges vary by campus.

careers.heading: Career pathways in research, diagnostics, regulatory and agro-industry
careers.intro: Postgraduates in Plant Pathology possess specialized skills essential for crop loss mitigation, seed health compliance, mushroom production, and pesticide development.

roles.title: Scientist (Plant Pathology) via ARS
roles.description: Lead research projects on crop disease resistance, pathogen genomics, epidemiology and climate-resilient management at ICAR research centres.

roles.title: Assistant Professor / KVK Subject Matter Specialist
roles.description: Educate undergraduate agricultural students and provide diagnostic field advisories to farmers facing disease outbreaks.

roles.title: Plant Quarantine & Inspection Officer
roles.description: Ensure consignments of imported seeds, plants and agricultural produce are free from foreign pathogens under the Plant Quarantine (Regulation of Import into India) Order.

roles.title: Seed Health Analyst & Certification Officer
roles.description: Conduct seed testing for seed-borne fungal, bacterial and viral pathogens in state seed certification labs and multinational seed corporations.

roles.title: Fungicide Product Development Specialist
roles.description: Direct bio-efficacy trials, resistance monitoring studies and registration dossiers for novel fungicidal molecules and biologicals.

roles.title: Commercial Mushroom Cultivation Consultant
roles.description: Design commercial spawn production facilities, compost formulations and environmental control systems for button, oyster and medicinal mushrooms.

faqs.question: What is the scope of M.Sc. Plant Pathology compared to M.Sc. Agronomy?
faqs.answer: While Agronomy focuses on overall field crop production, soil management and cultural practices, Plant Pathology is a specialized branch of plant protection dedicated to disease diagnostics, microbiological analysis, fungicide development and plant quarantine compliance.

faqs.question: Which government exams can I take after M.Sc. Plant Pathology?
faqs.answer: Graduates can appear for ASRB ARS Scientist and NET exams, State PSC exams for Agricultural Officer and Assistant Director (Plant Protection), SSC examinations for Plant Quarantine Inspector (DPPQS), and National Seeds Corporation (NSC) Quality Control officers.

faqs.question: Can I work in seed companies after doing M.Sc. in Plant Pathology?
faqs.answer: Yes. Seed corporations recruit plant pathologists extensively for seed health testing, seed treatment formulation, screening breeding germplasm for disease resistance, and ensuring domestic and export quarantine compliance.

faqs.question: Is laboratory work mandatory during M.Sc. Plant Pathology?
faqs.answer: Yes. Plant Pathology involves significant laboratory work, including pathogen isolation, pure culture maintenance, staining, microscopy, molecular testing (PCR) and fungicide bioassays alongside field experimental plots.
